parityBaseline: starci-academy CourseCatalogPage at mtp/9a1934231, rendered in production at academy.starci.org/vi/courses

workItems.owns: the /courses route, its discovery toolbar, its course collection and its pager
workItems.note: Net-new: the target's app router has only authentication, dashboard and profile.

evidence.claim: No /courses route exists in the target, so this page is net-new rather than a repair.
The legacy catalog owns a 350ms debounced search, a curated COURSE_ORDER client re-sort, PAGE_SIZE 9 and a grid/line view persisted at starci.course.catalogView.
Each card enriches a presentational CourseCard with a per-course coursePricePreview loyalty price, guarded by loyaltyPending to stop an N-card price flash, plus an AddToCartButton.
PaginationPageFilters already exposes search, so catalog search requires no backend enabler.
CourseEntity exposes coverImageUrl, originalPrice, enrollmentCount, isEnrolled, pricingPhases and valuePropositions.
ValuePropositionEntity.text with orderIndex is the truthful source of the production card's three check bullets.
The target's courses document selects nine fields, omitting valuePropositions and all price-phase data; its hook exposes no search parameter.

myCourses query1 selects completionPercent and query2 selects thumbnailUrl plus content and challenge counters, which proves a real source for the selected direction's owned-course progress and artwork.
price-discount-line exists; there is no catalog, cart, pagination or cover-image vocabulary anywhere in the target.
Cart appears only as a ShellNav icon and an Icon name. There is no myCart query and no add or remove mutation.

unknowns: pageNumber base: the backend documents PaginationPageFilters.pageNumber as 1-based while the legacy hook passes a 0-based index. Preview must resolve this against a live query rather than copying the legacy call.
The target has no cart data layer, so the production card's cart action cannot be built truthfully in this scope.
Whether valuePropositions returns a reliable three rows per course or must be sliced for card density.
Whether enrolment grouping should override the curated COURSE_ORDER the legacy page deliberately applies.

directions.thesis: Reproduce the named production catalog exactly: one discovery toolbar above a three-column grid, and a card that carries the whole sales pitch.
directions.primaryCta: Per-card course action (Tiếp tục học for an owned course, Xem khóa học otherwise)
tradeoffs: Strongest fidelity to the reference the user named, at the cost of the largest new vocabulary surface.
Tall cards: three value propositions plus description plus price plus two actions make a three-column row very deep.

directions.thesis: The catalog mixes courses the learner already owns with courses they can buy, and the production page makes them read each card's button to tell which is which. Group by enrolment first, so section membership answers that question and each section keeps one CTA meaning.
directions.primaryCta: Tiếp tục học in the owned section; Xem khóa học leads the discover section
tradeoffs: A returning learner reaches their unfinished course without scanning, and each section's CTA carries one meaning.
It departs from the named production render, which is the opposite of pure parity, and it competes with the curated COURSE_ORDER.
legacyDivergence: Production renders one ungrouped grid; this direction introduces two titled groups keyed on isEnrolled.
Owned courses lose the full sales pitch and gain a progress meter instead.
Value propositions move behind a disclosure in the discover group rather than always being visible.

contracts.why: The payable price leads while original price and discount qualify that same commerce fact on one wrapping line.
Owned and purchasable courses answer different questions, so each keeps its own titled group and one CTA meaning.
The promises stay available but stop competing with price for first read in a multi-column grid.
Query, result count and layout choice all narrow the same list, so they stay on one control row above it.
